# Education in Nigeria
Nigeria's education system is structured into primary, secondary, and tertiary levels. Primary education begins around age 5 and lasts six years; students graduate with a first school-leaving certificate and take a Common Entrance Examination for secondary school admission. The Universal Basic Education (UBE) program, formed in 1999, makes nine years of schooling (six years primary and three years junior secondary) free, compulsory, and a right for every child. Secondary education, following the UBE, spans six years divided into Junior Secondary School (JSS) and Senior Secondary School (SSS). Core subjects include English, Mathematics, Economics, and Civic Education, with electives available. Federal government colleges ("unity schools") provide model education, while state-sponsored and private schools vary in quality and resources. Promotional exams culminate in the Senior Secondary Certificate Examination (SSCE), administered by the West African Examination Council (WAEC). Advanced level programs like the Interim Joint Matriculation Board (IJMB) facilitate university direct entry.
Tertiary education includes public and private universities, polytechnics, monotechnics, and colleges of education, with 153 universities registered by the Nigerian Universities Commission. Admission requires SSCE credit passes and scores on the Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) exams. Universities offer varied lengths for degrees depending on fields of study. Vocational education, overseen by the National Board for Technical Education and NABTEB, includes technical certificates and apprenticeships but faces challenges such as teacher shortages and outdated curricula. Informal education and literacy programs play significant roles but are underfunded. Female education has improved, supported by government and NGO initiatives, though barriers persist, especially in rural areas. Literacy rates remain low with regional disparities; efforts focus on enhancing both general and digital literacy nationwide.
